newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria institute warns of currency board failure.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria institute warns of currency board failure.

text.p: The Economy Institute at the Bulgarian Academy of Sciences warned on Monday that corrupt business interests could thwart government plans to reform the economy through a restrictive monetary regime.

"There are many groups combining political and business interests which will do everything possible to limit the efficiency of the currency board system and to discredit it in the process of operation," said the institute in its annual report published in the Pari daily.

Bulgaria pledged to introduce a fixed exchange rate regime known as a currency board in June to restore confidence in its financial system under a $510 million 14-month standby accord signed with the International Monetary Fund last month.

The IMF board is expected to review preparations for the currency board and consider disbursing the first tranche of the standby on Friday. The cabinet said last week it had met all of the conditions required to prepare the system's implementation.

"Application of the currency board system in Bulgaria will be difficult and painful, especially in the current situation of complete economic destabilisation and humiliating impoverishment of thousands of people," said the report.
Depreciation of the lev and galloping inflation have eroded people's income to the extent that two thirds of the population live below the existential minimum.

Cumulative inflation for the first two months of this year stood at 392 percent. The lev, after hitting a 3,000 per dollar record low in February from 600 at the beginning of January, has recovered to around 1,600 now.

The currency board system would require levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank and preventing the printing of money.

"Large scale criminal misappropriation of funds has caused irreparable damage to the economy. But the price is paid by ordinary taxpayers and depositors whom the government now asks again to bear with new destitution," said the institute.

Bulgaria's crisis is attributed to asset stripping of major state companies and siphoning of funds abroad by businessmen from the former communist party, now grouped into a handful of powerful firms that sprang up amid the legal and administrative chaos that followed the collapse of communism seven years ago.

"Market reform is strongly opposed by people united by corrupt motivation. These are economic groups and part of the state administration, which is incompetent, inefficient, disloyal and corrupt," said the institute.
The report called for a drastic reform and reduction of the state administration along with rapid liberalisation and privatisation of the economy regardless of the obstacles.

"Most dangerous are the group economic interests because of the substantial resources and interaction with other group interests, which can easily corrupt all parts of society. Their major arguments will be the difficulty of implementing the currency board and its social consequences," said the report.
Actions against crime and corruption will be presented as infringements of human rights and private enterprise, it added.

"If the state institutions do not take rapid and effective measures to overcome resistance of business group interests, they will neutralise the currency board, will discredit it and fail it. There should be no doubt in this," the report concluded. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
